title: bug: under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 the sh wrapper keeps empty, '.', relative and in-project PATH entries, so its bare-name tools (git, dirname, uname, serena) and a standalone moe-call.sh can run project copies
description:
Found by CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), the epic-final adversarial review. It covers residuals 1 and 2 in architect-54e5eb09's comment-1deae51a and the "POSIX pwsh does not prepend the pinned dir" residual from task-64809b19's review.

Evidence at 28df02f7: moe-agent.sh under the marker pins node and python3 (protected_pin_interpreters) and the agent CLI (protected_path_lookup), but it leaves PATH as inherited. Every other bare-name command, such as git, dirname, uname, mktemp and the Serena binary, is still found by PATH lookup, so an empty, '.', relative or in-project entry reaches a project-planted copy. A standalone `scripts/moe-call.sh` under the marker runs `command -v node`, and only the wrapper's use_node prepend makes that safe. The pwsh (POSIX) path of moe-agent.ps1 aliases node but does not prepend its directory.

Fix direction: under the marker, rewrite PATH once, early, to the absolute entries outside the project (the same test protected_path_lookup applies), before any bare-name call. moe-call.sh does the same, or it refuses to run under the marker without a pinned node.
definitionOfDone: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, moe-agent.sh and moe-call.sh drop empty, '.', relative and in-project PATH entries before their first bare-name command; a planted <project>/git (or dirname) on a '.' entry never runs, proved by a bash row like protected-agent-command.test.mjs N5.
The ps1 POSIX (pwsh) path gives child processes the pinned node directory first, or the row documents why it is not needed.
Legacy seats are unchanged; parity-check.sh and the launcher suites exit 0.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1, sh wrapper. Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, scripts/moe-agent.sh rewrites PATH before its first bare-name command. That first command is the dirname on the SCRIPT_DIR line. git and sed (in moe_wrapper_in_worktree) and the ROOT_DIR dirname also run today before the marker is read.
(1) Move normalize_path (with its two comment lines) and protected_trusted_dir (with its comment line) up to just after the colour variables, byte for byte, so the early block can call them. Both use builtins only.
(2) Add protected_scrub_path, with a comment naming task-0b2ea570.
- Its arguments are project real paths. With none, use one empty project: protected_trusted_dir then still drops empty, '.', relative and nonexistent entries.
- Split PATH with `IFS=: read -r -a`.
- Keep an entry only when protected_trusted_dir accepts it for every project. Keep the real path it prints, in order; duplicates may stay.
- If nothing is kept, print the existing python3 MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND line to stderr and exit 1. That line is always true here, because python3 is pinned only from PATH.
- Otherwise export PATH.
- Never export an empty PATH: bash then searches the current directory, which is the project. Probed on bash 5.2: `env PATH= bash -c dirname` runs ./dirname, and so does `unset PATH` inside bash.
(3) Directly after the function, add a block guarded by `[ "${MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED:-}" = 1 ]`. Use that guard because RUNTIME_PROTECTED is set lower down.
- Into a global array MOE_PROTECTED_PROJECTS, collect the real path, `cd -- "$(normalize_path "$tok")" && pwd -P`, of every token that follows a -p or --project token in "$@". The parser keeps the last such value, and every value it can take is such a token.
- Skip a token that does not resolve. protected_pin_interpreters refuses that seat before any helper or CLI runs.
- Then call the scrub.
(4) Call the scrub again right after the $HOME/.local/share/moe/npm/bin append: `[ "$RUNTIME_PROTECTED" != 1 ] || protected_scrub_path "${MOE_PROTECTED_PROJECTS[@]}"`. The wrapper's only other PATH write is use_node's pinned directory, which is already trusted.
Error handling:
- An unresolvable candidate is skipped.
- When no entry survives, the refusal exits 1 before the EXIT trap and create_secure_temp exist, so there is nothing to deregister or clean.
- When a tool is missing from every trusted entry, the existing ROOT_DIR dirname assignment fails under set -e (exit 127) before any helper runs. Probed.
Constraints:
- Builtins only, up to and including the scrub.
- Bash 3.2 must parse and run it: CI parses this file with macOS /bin/bash 3.2, and JetBrains runs Mac seats through it. So no mapfile, no declare -A, no new ${x,,}, and no quoted heredoc inside $( ).
- No new MOE_ code, because parity-check compares the code sets.
- Legacy (the marker unset or not exactly '1') runs none of this.
- Leave the NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath comment and its ps1 twin as they are.
Reference: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/0b2ea570-plan/proto-moe-agent.sh.diff; the suite run with it gave 119 tests, 93 pass, 0 fail, 26 skip. Edit with the Edit tool, then run `bash -n`.
implementationPlan.note: Moved normalize_path and protected_trusted_dir byte-for-byte above SCRIPT_DIR. Added builtin-only multi-project pre-scan and PATH scrub, guarded by exact marker, and re-scrub after npm/bin append. Empty survivor set exits 1 with existing python3 refusal. MOE_PROTECTED_PROJECTS is initialized inside the guard so legacy runs no new executable code. bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh exits 0; joined behavioral gate remains step 4.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1 for moe-call.sh, DoD 2, and the doc.
(1) scripts/moe-call.sh.
- Define a byte-identical copy of protected_trusted_dir, with its comment line, just above the existing `if [ "${MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED:-}" = 1 ]` block. S3 pins the copy.
- In that branch, after PYTHON_CMD="", resolve PROJECT's real path with `cd -- "$PROJECT" && pwd -P`. A failure leaves it empty.
- Keep each PATH entry protected_trusted_dir accepts, and only when the project resolved: without a real path, no entry can be proven outside the project. Keep the real paths in order.
- If nothing is kept, run `echo "Error: node not found" >&2; exit 1`, the existing line. Otherwise export PATH.
- All of this runs before find_node and before the first node exec.
- The file runs under set -euo pipefail, and macOS CI runs moe-call.test.mjs with /bin/bash 3.2. So expand the array as ${a[@]+"${a[@]}"} and keep every test that can fail inside an && list.
- Reference: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/0b2ea570-plan/proto-moe-call.sh.diff.
(2) scripts/moe-agent.ps1: right after `Set-Alias -Name node -Value $script:MoeNode -Scope Script` in the protected block, add a two-line comment and exactly the S2 statement. Change nothing else, and keep the BOM and LF endings.
- Why POSIX: there the agent CLI's `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang, and every other child, finds node by name. sh's use_node prepends for the same reason.
- Why not Windows: there the .cmd shim's node lookup is cmd.exe's, which NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath covers (row C2). A Windows prepend would also put the node folder ahead of fx.trusted in rows A1 and T3 on hosts whose npm prefix is that folder. Windows '.', relative and in-project entries stay with task-3acf7f79.
(3) docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, Protected control plane bullet. Replace "The launchers' own lookups through such PATH entries are open: task-0b2ea570 (sh) and task-3acf7f79 (ps1)." with these facts, keeping the bullet's ~120-column wrap:
- Under the marker, moe-agent.sh and moe-call.sh rewrite PATH, before their first bare-name command, to its absolute entries outside the project.
- A rewrite that keeps no entry refuses, because an empty PATH makes bash search the current directory.
- So neither they nor the agent CLI they start finds a tool through a '.', relative or in-project entry.
- The ps1 launcher's own lookups stay open (task-3acf7f79). On POSIX it puts the pinned node's directory first.
Error handling: both sh refusals exit 1 with an existing line. The ps1 statement runs only after a successful pin; Stop-MoeProtectedAgent already exits on a failed one.

Architecture records the sh guarantee and ps1 residual. bash -n moe-call exits 0; ps1 retains efbbbf BOM and zero CR bytes. Serena excludes docs/, so documentation edited with main apply_patch tool.

comments.author: worker-c9368191
comments.content:
Planner input from CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), epic-final review, finding 4 (LOW). It belongs with this row's "PATH as inherited" class.

Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-call.sh never remove `NODE_OPTIONS` or `NODE_PATH` (grep finds no hit in any of the three at 28df02f7). The IDEs do remove both before spawning the installed daemon: MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt 576-581, and MoeDaemonClient.ts 537 and 562.

So the pinned node that the wrapper runs (the proxy, moe-call, helper .mjs scripts) still honours an inherited `NODE_OPTIONS=--require ./x.js`. That path is resolved against the seat's cwd, which is the project.

The values come from the user's own environment rather than the repository, which is why this is LOW. Still, for parity, drop both variables in the same early protected block that rewrites PATH, in sh and ps1, and add one row that sets NODE_OPTIONS to a planted require and asserts it never loads.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 (exactly '1'), scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-call.sh rewrite PATH to its absolute, existing entries whose real path is outside the project. They keep the real paths in their original order. moe-agent.sh does this before its first bare-name command and again after its npm/bin append; moe-call.sh does it before node. So no empty, '.', relative or in-project entry reaches a project-planted dirname, git, sed, mktemp, basename, bash or node, whether the wrapper or the agent CLI it starts looks the name up. A rewrite that keeps nothing refuses, exiting 1 with an existing line, instead of exporting an empty PATH. On POSIX pwsh, moe-agent.ps1 puts the pinned node's directory first on PATH. Legacy runs (the marker unset or not exactly '1') are unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Scrub after the project is resolved: rejected, because dirname, git, sed, mktemp and basename run before then. (2) A $PWD fallback candidate: rejected, because it drops $HOME entries when the cwd is not the project.
